 The structure of each node in the Dynamic Segment Tree can contain the following information:
 - Start and end coordinates of the segment
 - Length of the segment
 - Pointers to left and right child nodes
 - Other necessary information for tree operations
 
 The operations can be implemented as follows:
 
 1. \texttt{Insert(x, y)}:
  To insert a segment (x, y) into the Dynamic Segment Tree, we start at the root and recursively traverse the tree to find the correct position for insertion based on the length of segments. This operation will have an expected time complexity of $O(\log n)$.
 
 2. \texttt{Delete(x, y)}:
  To delete a segment (x, y) from the Dynamic Segment Tree, we need to search for the segment with coordinates (x, y) and remove it from the tree. This operation will also have an expected time complexity of $O(\log n)$.
 
 3. \texttt{Find-Min()}:
  To find the shortest segment in the Dynamic Segment Tree, we simply need to return the segment stored at the bottom-left node of the tree, as it will contain the smallest length. This operation can be done in constant time.
 
 4. Linear Construction Time:
  The Dynamic Segment Tree can be built in linear time by initially constructing a balanced binary search tree based on the lengths of segments, and then converting it into a Dynamic Segment Tree. This process can be done in $O(n)$ time complexity.
 
 The Dynamic Segment Tree allows for efficient insertion, deletion, and search operations on segments while maintaining the required time complexities for the specified operations.
